diagram_math_checks.justification: Example and def-finite-markov-decision-process give S={s} and A(s)={a,b}. The sole circle is s and the two rectangles are action nodes a,b, as explicitly distinguished in Remarks; s->a and s->b are choice arrows, not stochastic transitions or an asserted policy.

Example and F1 specify reward 0 and deterministic return to s for both actions. By the joint-law convention in def-finite-markov-decision-process, p(s,0|s,a)=p(s,0|s,b)=1. Each labeled return arrow therefore starts at its respective action rectangle and ends at s; the final native view independently confirms both arrowheads at s.

With gamma=1/2, r=0 and P(s|s,a)=P(s|s,b)=1, the policy Bellman formula gives T^pi v(s)=v(s)/2 for either deterministic policy. Verification 1.1 solves v=0, uniquely consistent with the local contraction theorem; the optimality formula then gives Q(s,a)=Q(s,b)=0. No figure label implies unequal values or a selected policy.

alg-policy-iteration step 2 retains the current maximizing action, and step 3 stops when the policy is unchanged, so starting a stops after one exact evaluation. Verification 2.2 explicitly defines the alternative switching rule, producing a,b,a,b indefinitely. The diagram depicts the common MDP only and asserts neither that every arbitrary tie rule cycles nor that both actions are selected by one deterministic policy.
